subject.title: fix(gateway): throttle rapid process restarts before sidecar startup

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a global persistent process-start throttle for external crash loops, and if so should it cover the full startup lifecycle rather than only sidecar loading?
rationale: The desired availability tradeoff and lifecycle boundary determine whether the correct fix is a narrow shared-state throttle, a different recovery mechanism, or continued work under the broader crash-recovery proposal.

options.title: Adopt a bounded full-startup throttle
options.body: Rework the PR on current main using shared SQLite state and cover the startup stages that can trigger the reported external restart loop.

options.title: Keep recovery limited to explicit restart flows
options.body: Do not add a global process-start delay; continue relying on restart-sentinel and targeted root-cause fixes for individual startup failures.

options.title: Route it into graduated recovery design
options.body: Defer this first-rung mitigation until it is designed together with the broader recovery policy in the canonical crash-recovery discussion.

recommendation.title: Adopt a bounded full-startup throttle
recommendation.body: Rework the PR on current main using shared SQLite state and cover the startup stages that can trigger the reported external restart loop.
